idiom_name: Rack middleware stack (use) with SimpleDelegator / Delegator for per-object gates
implementation_notes: Ruby's standard library provides the proxy: SimpleDelegator forwards every supported call to the wrapped object, so a gate subclasses it and overrides only the guarded method; in web stacks the chain is Rack's middleware stack, where use Gate wraps the application and each middleware's call(env) either short-circuits with a response tuple or passes control inward with @app.call(env). What replaces the classic structure: the stdlib delegation classes and Rack's builder replace hand-written forwarding and a hand-built chain - a gate is one class with call, constructed with the inner app - and method_missing with respond_to_missing? remains the fallback when the guarded object cannot be delegated to. Keep the verified identity in the Rack env (or the delegator's own state) and let each layer verify again.
pitfalls: Rack middleware must return the exact [status, headers, body] tuple; a gate returning a bare body or nil breaks the server and can be read as a successful response.
Middleware that replaces a body must close the one it consumed; leaking streaming bodies leaks sockets in long-lived servers.
SimpleDelegator dispatches through method_missing, so a gate subclass that forgets to override a guarded method silently delegates, and __setobj__ lets the delegate be retargeted at runtime.
